processing: When made as white tea, as is usual for the class, the leaf is withered and dried without a kill-green or rolling. The same local leaf can also go into other tea types.
harvest_season: Little is documented for this tea specifically; as with other Yunnan white teas, spring pickings are the ones most sought after.
appearance_dry: Typically plump, downy buds or bud-and-leaf sets, silver-grey with darker leaf where leaf is included.
appearance_liquor: Typically a clear pale yellow to yellow-green.
appearance_wet: Typically large, soft buds and leaves in a muted olive green.
taste_profile: Little is written about this tea's taste on its own; large-leaf Yunnan whites in general tend toward soft honey and hay with a gentle sweetness.

brewing.notes: General guidance for large-bud Yunnan white tea rather than a local rule. Big buds open slowly, so give them time.

vintage_note: Little is documented about how this tea is dated. As with other Yunnan white teas, expect it sold by harvest year, either fresh or pressed and kept for some years; ask for the year and the picking.
description:
Jinggu Dabai means, roughly, Jinggu big white: a white tea name tied to Jinggu county in Pu'er, Yunnan. The name works as a local leaf type and as a county brand at the same time, which is worth knowing when you see it on a label.

Details of how it is made are thin. Treated as a white tea, it would follow the usual path for the class: withering and drying, without the heat fix and rolling that shape green teas.

In the cup, expect what is typical of large-bud Yunnan whites rather than a documented signature: soft sweetness, honey and hay. Water a little off the boil and unhurried steeps suit big buds.

Because the county name now covers a wide area, the label alone says little about which village or garden the leaf came from. Ask for the harvest year and the place. For a closer look at the area's best-known white, try Yangta Dabai from the same county.
history: Little is documented about the early history of this tea under this name. The firmest date is recent: on 22 March 2023 Jinggu county presented Jinggu Dabai as its regional public brand at a press conference in Yunnan. At that point the planting was described as about 200,000 mu across 10 townships, with more than 120,000 tea farmers.
